gaps.sentence: It was the most ___ (FORGET) trip of my life.
gaps.hint: negative adjective: too good to forget
gaps.explanation: 'Unforgettable' = impossible to forget; 'forgetful' describes a person who forgets.

gaps.sentence: The new bypass will be ___ (BENEFIT) to thousands of commuters.
gaps.explanation: 'Be beneficial to' — the adjective follows the verb 'be'.

gaps.sentence: The storm caused serious ___ (DESTROY) along the coast.
gaps.explanation: After the adjective 'serious' a noun is needed: destruction (-tion noun).

gaps.sentence: The instructions were unclear, so I had to ___ them completely (WRITE).
gaps.hint: write again — unclear the first time (re-); base verb needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix re- means again: rewrite. A base verb is needed after 'had to'.

gaps.sentence: We had a ___ view of the coast from the plane (SPECTACLE).
gaps.explanation: The adjective of 'spectacle' is spectacular; it modifies the noun 'view'.

gaps.sentence: It is highly ___ that she will win — she leads by ten points (LIKE).
gaps.explanation: The context shows probability, so 'likely' is needed; 'unlikely' would contradict her lead.

gaps.sentence: She gave a brief ___ of her plans (DESCRIBE).
gaps.explanation: After 'a brief' a noun is needed: description (-tion).

gaps.sentence: She has been a loyal ___ (EMPLOY) of the firm for twenty years.
gaps.hint: person needed: someone who works for the firm
gaps.explanation: An employee works for a company; 'employment' is the uncountable state of having a job.
